name: Nebula Aura Theme
description: Four Nebula Aura colour themes (Light, Dark, Violet, Midnight) mapped onto the PI-Desktop design tokens, with the host's hardcoded neutrals re-pointed at the palette and the Git Lens + File Manager plugin panels adapted (the file manager's JSON viewer included). Soft aura palette, translucent accent user bubbles, elevated assistant cards, accent-tinted hairlines and code blocks. UI font = Maple Mono NF + 腾祥爱情体简 (install them; nothing is bundled).

en.name: Nebula Aura Theme
en.description: Four Nebula Aura colour themes (Light, Dark, Violet, Midnight) mapped onto the PI-Desktop design tokens: soft aura glow with a faint star field, translucent accent user bubbles, elevated assistant cards, accent-tinted hairlines and code blocks.

author: moyining (palette: Nebula Aura Theme, MIT, luismpenholato)
safetyNotes: Pure styling. The plugin contributes four global themes (CSS only). No network, file, clipboard, or agent access.
changelog: Release 1.6.0: the plugin adaptation is re-verified against the real plugin packages and the host's own appearance API, and three gaps are closed. (1) pi.file-manager's JSON viewer gained its four missing syntax colours — the plugin hardcodes Atom One's #e45649 / #50a14f / #986801 / #a626a4 in --json-key / --json-string / --json-number / --json-literal, which nothing in the previous mapping reached. They now follow the palette: Light takes the same H and S as --ds-error / --ds-success / --ds-warning / --ds-purple with the lightness reduced until each clears 4.8:1 on --bg (measured 4.80 / 4.83 / 4.84 / 4.84:1 — the raw tokens were 4.47 / 3.23 / 3.26 / 4.34:1, under the 4.5:1 bar for 11.5 px code text), while the dark-based variants use their tokens verbatim (Dark 4.76 / 8.99 / 7.48 / 6.02:1, Violet 5.96 / 10.97 / 8.08 / 5.50:1, Midnight 6.51 / 11.82 / 10.79 / 6.82:1). One component literal the plugin writes by hand — the JSON expand row .json-more = #4aa3d9 — is now var(--accent) (4.80 / 5.85 / 6.20 / 6.05:1). (2) Cascade fix: the mapping selector is now `:root[data-base]:has(.tree-size)` (0,3,0), keeping the ungated selector for the frame before data-base exists. Measured in Chromium 148 against the plugin's real stylesheet: the old (0,2,0) selector TIED with the plugin's own `:root[data-base=light]` block, so a sheet injected before the plugin's own <style> (its bundle appends one at init) lost the ENTIRE light mapping — reproduced as --bg #fafafa / --json-key #e45649, now #F7F6FC / #BD4253; the fix wins in both document orders on all four variants (the dark-based variants never showed it — their own block is `:root`, 0,1,0). (3) Two facts corrected in the comments and README: pi.file-manager 0.3.1 is shipped BUILT INTO the host at resources/plugins/pi.file-manager, byte-identical to the marketplace copy apart from line endings, and its dormancy is now stated from the host's own code — app.getAppearance resolves to { theme, base, locale, pluginTheme{id,base,css} } in host 0.14.8, the plugin reads only base, and the host injects no CSS into plugin documents at all (0 insertCSS in app.asar). Leak check re-run in the same harness, and again with a positive control: 0 of the 30 plugin short names resolve in a host-like document (adding a .segmented element resolves 17 of them, adding a .tree-size element resolves 19, removing it returns the count to 0). (4) Three further defects were measured and fixed in Chromium 148 before this build shipped: the host backdrop's background-color is now cancelled inside a plugin document, so Git Lens is no longer painted #F2F1F8 / #1A1B26 / #171320 / #0B1020 behind its surfaces but the mapped #F7F6FC / #222433 / #1F1A2E / #0F1628 (deleting that one new rule through CSSOM restores the bleed in all four variants); pi.file-manager's markdown preview hardcodes the same #4aa3d9 as its JSON expand row, so .md-link now follows var(--accent) alongside .json-more; and the pi-plugin-panel-chrome page colours carry this variant's literal as a fallback, because where --ds-* is undefined the !important re-pointing became invalid-at-computed-value-time and erased the preload's inline colours instead of leaving them alone. Release 1.5.0: the two official marketplace plugins are now adapted to the palette. pi.gitlens (Git Lens 0.2.7) applies the active plugin theme inside its own document (renderer/appearance-boot.js injects app.getAppearance().pluginTheme and sets data-theme), and every one of its surfaces reads one of 23 short custom props (only its two :root blocks hold literals), so those props are mapped to this palette: bg/group/inset/hover/separator/track/thumb/accent/on-accent/success/warning/error and the four text levels. Measured in a simulated Git Lens document: header #f2f3f5 -> #F7F6FC, cards #ffffff -> #FCFBFF, diff panel #eef0f2 -> #D8D5E6, added-line green #248a3d -> #3D9A6E, deleted-line red #d70015 -> #C04A5A, primary button #1a1c1f -> #6B5BD4 with #F2F1F8 ink; radius/motion/font tokens are left to the plugin. pi.file-manager (0.3.1) reads app.getAppearance but ignores the pluginTheme payload and sets data-base instead of data-theme, so no theme can reach its document today; its own 15 props are nevertheless mapped from this variant's literal palette (var(--ds-*) cannot resolve there) and gated on its unique .tree-size, ready to take effect as soon as the plugin applies the CSS - the README carries the upstream patch. Every plugin short name is declared only inside a :has(<signature>) block, verified to leak nothing into the host document (the host has Tailwind utilities reading var(--fg) and var(--surface-hover)): none of the mapped short names resolve in the host doc while all of them resolve in the plugin doc. Also overrides the host panel chrome's inline page colours (--pi-plugin-panel-page-background/-foreground) with the palette. Release 1.4.0: colour audit of the host sheet (see README). Release 1.3.0: no bundled fonts. Release 1.0.0: first release.
